params.prompt:
PRODUCTION GAME SPRITE ATLAS for Coaster Grove. Use the supplied original game assets as EXACT visual style reference. Authentic late1990s PC theme park management game PIXEL ART. These are miniature functional sprites, simple chunky square pixels and hard stair-step edges, 2-3 flat palette shades per material, dark modest outlines. Keep low detail that is readable when very small. No smooth illustration, no concept art, no realistic rendering, no texture, no gradients, no antialiasing, no blur, no ambient occlusion, no glow, no ground shadows. Isometric ORTHOGRAPHIC 2:1 projection, camera azimuth45degrees and elevation26.565degrees. Every ground edge runs TWO horizontal screen pixels for ONE vertical pixel, no converging perspective.
Entire background exactly uniform bright MAGENTA #FF00FF, including gaps, holes and between every object. No gradients in background. No text or labels, no cell borders, no grid, no ground tiles, no attached landscape, no scenery, no decorative bases. Each object fully isolated and complete inside one cell with at least12percent clear margin. Do not allow any part to touch a cell edge. Crisp original objects matching reference palette coral-red, teal, cream, gold, restrained brown; launch purple must be DEEP VIOLET #61428C, never magenta.
EXACT layout FOUR equal columns by THREE equal rows, twelve equal square cells. All12cars same physical game scale. Each cell represents a64x64 logicalpixel canvas enlarged nearest-neighbor, each car occupies roughly40x30logicalpixels, simple large color clusters, same pixel density as supplied small coaster cars.
The four columns show FOUR views of the same car of each row: column1 FRONT points diagonally SCREEN LOWER RIGHT (SE), column2 FRONT points SCREEN LOWER LEFT (SW), column3 FRONT points SCREEN UPPER LEFT (NW), column4 FRONT points SCREEN UPPER RIGHT (NE). Each car has a clear pointed front nose and blunt back, and faces exact indicated screen direction. Rear views must expose REAR backs of seats and rear of chassis, never another front view. There is no train, no track, no support and no rider; only ONE complete separate car percell.
Every car has exactly TWO clearly separated transverse BENCH ROWS one behind another along its long axis, each row wide enough for two people: FOUR seats total, obvious cream cushions with dark seat gaps and simple lap bars. Make recognizably little rollercoaster cars, not buses, road cars, boats, or huge illustrations. Dark small rail-wheel assemblies beneath chassis.
ROW1: modern STEEL coaster car. Rounded coral-red aerodynamic nose and red sides, dark-teal undercarriage, cream two-row seats. Match existing car with a more clearly readable two-row seating layout.
ROW2: traditional WOODEN coaster car. Boxier warm walnut-brown body, golden-yellow slim trim, black undercarriage, cream two-row seats. Small wood panel clusters, no texture. Clearly squared front ledge unlike red rounded car.
ROW3: LAUNCH coaster car. Low sleek angular turquoise nose and turquoise body, deep-violet purple #61428C seat backs and side accent, charcoal undercarriage, cream two-row cushions. Clearly a distinct sharper sporty outline but same game size.
Exactly12 isolated cars.

processing: Technical processing only: atlas-cell crops (structures row split moved into empty gutter y600, parts first split y628 to retain complete tower finials), magenta color key to binary alpha, transparent trim, isotropic nearest-neighbor normalization, fixed logical canvases and pivots, exact4x nearest-neighbor PNG copies. Pirate ship translated2logicalpixels to align hub. No visual features painted, filled, or synthesized in code. Deep violet launch accents are preserved by a narrow bright-magenta key.

visualReview.result: 24 isolated, readable game sprites with style and palette consistent with pixel-v2. All four car orientations and three types are distinct. Two transverse cream bench rows are visible. All six modular components are isolated without the other moving or static half. Tower finials retained after gutter correction.
limitations: Individual passenger slots within each bench are not separated; two bench rows are the readable seating unit.
Modular pirate frame/ship are broadside and do not reproduce the complete static icon exact angled geometry.
A single swing-chair view is supplied; orbit and depth ordering remain renderer work.
These are fixed pixel projection assets; exact analytical 2:1 geometry and intercomponent perspective were not machine-verified.
